s1.quote: The remains of the Pendleton lie in around 40 feet of water off Pollock Rip Shoal … it is also a hazard to divers. … Diving on the Pendleton is allowed as the wreck is marked an Exempted Wreck Site by the state of Massachusetts.

s2.quote: The remains of the wreck lie in about 30 feet of water off Monomoy.

access.value: Exempted wreck site in Massachusetts; diving allowed but removing or disturbing wreckage is unlawful

hazards.text: Jagged metal left over from the blast
Rough water; suited to experienced divers

summary.text: Shallow, broken remains of a wrecked ship's stern section off Monomoy near Chatham, Cape Cod. Rough water and sharp wreckage make it a dive for experienced divers; it may be dived but not disturbed.

sites.name: Brother Jonathan

s1.quote: a depth of 275 feet (84 m) … About 4.5 mi (7.2 km) SW of Point St. George … rocky passageways, underwater currents, and underwater darkness

s2.quote: it located Brother Jonathan 260 feet down, in murky waters ten miles northwest of Crescent City

s3.quote: Although the wreck was not particularly deep (about 272 feet)

summary.text: Historic steamer lost on the rocks off Point St. George near Crescent City in 1865 and found by minisub in 1993. It lies roughly 260-275 ft down in murky, current-swept water, well beyond recreational limits.

sites.depthNote: Reported 260 to 275 ft depending on source

s1.quote: about 40 feet of water … The wreck was covered in 'hundreds of thousands, if not millions' of zebra mussels

s2.quote: 45 feet (15 meters) … over 200,000 gallons of hazardous material … diving and exploration are highly regulated

hazards.text: Hazardous cargo leaking from the hull

summary.text: Tank barge lost in Lake Erie in 1937 and rediscovered in 2015, resting in roughly 40-45 ft of water. Its leftover hazardous cargo made it a priority wreck for NOAA, so access is tightly regulated.

s1.quote: Depth at Wreck Site: 12.8 m / 42 ft … Approximately 10 miles southeast of Chicago, off the coast of Whiting, Indiana

s2.quote: The remains of the David Dows, nicknamed the Queen of the Lakes, can be found in 42 feet of water … Over the years, divers have visited the Queen of the Lakes

summary.text: Remains of the five-masted schooner nicknamed the Queen of the Lakes, lying in about 42 ft of southern Lake Michigan off Whiting, Indiana. It is a long-visited, moderately shallow wreck reached by boat.

s1.quote: Resting in 76 feet (23.2 m) of water near a shipping lane … to within 45 feet (13.7 m) of the lake's surface … her wreck is disarticulated and scattered over a wide area

summary.text: Large Lake Erie freighter sunk in a 1944 collision and later dynamited as a navigation hazard, leaving scattered wreckage in about 76 ft of water beside a shipping lane. Rated an intermediate dive.

s1.quote: Depth at Wreck Site: 24 m / 80 ft … upside-down in silty mud; access is possible for technical divers

s2.quote: 79′ depth … Sports divers reported finding the Gerkin using a sonar device in 2009.

highlights.text: Upside-down hull partly buried in silt

summary.text: Capsized sand dredge about 7 miles off Erie, Pennsylvania, lying upside down in silt at roughly 80 ft. Found by sonar in 2009 and dived since.

s1.quote: It lies about 20 miles (32 km) off Dunkirk resting in 170 feet (52 m) of cold freshwater
It lies at a depth of approximately 240 feet (73 m) … approximately 14 miles (23 km) northeast of Boston Harbor … visited by divers on July 20, 2003

s2.quote: 240′ … 150 tons of ammunition, which included obsolete pyrotechnics, black powder, and 50-caliber projectiles

summary.text: Navy lighter that sank in 1944 while carrying ammunition for disposal, now lying near 240 ft about 14 miles off Boston. Found in 2002 and dived by deep technical divers.

s1.quote: The shipwreck is in 30 ft (9.1 m) of water, and is an easy scuba dive mission. … the hull is mostly buried in the sand, small artifacts and copper spikes may still be found.

s2.quote: 30' Maximum … Graves Island, Manchester, MA, just off east side of island … Hull is broken up and mostly buried in sand.

highlights.text: Copper spikes and small artifacts in the sand

summary.text: Broken-up remains of a burned 19th-century ship of the line off Graves Island, Manchester-by-the-Sea, in about 30 ft of water. The hull is mostly sand-covered; copper spikes can still be found.

s1.quote: She lies in 450 feet (140 m) of water 16 miles northeast of Port Washington, Wisconsin.

s2.quote: nearly 500 feet of water … 16 miles northeast of Port Washington

summary.text: Freighter that sank in 1929 after a collision and now lies roughly 450-500 ft down, 16 miles off Port Washington, Wisconsin. Far beyond recreational limits, it has been surveyed with ROV and sonar.

s1.quote: The wreck is largely intact but is upside down and in about 77–80 feet (23–24 m) of water. … an active dive site for scuba divers and is now part of Michigan's underwater Preserve system.

s2.quote: She rests upside down on the bottom in about 80 feet of water. The bottom of the hull can be reached at 25 feet. … There is a 56 foot hole in the hull that permits entry to the hold area by qualified divers.

penetration.value: 56 ft hole in the hull allows entry to the hold for qualified divers

summary.text: Upside-down steel freighter lost in the 1913 Great Storm, lying in about 80 ft in Michigan's Sanilac Shores Underwater Preserve in Lake Huron. The hull bottom rises to 25 ft, and a large hole allows qualified divers into the hold.

s1.quote: It sits upright on the bottom of Lake Ontario in 117 feet (36 m) of water northeast of Pultneyville, New York. … Its deck and lower hull are intact. … one of the most accessible shipwrecks for recreational divers in the sanctuary.

s2.publisher: NOAA Office of National Marine Sanctuaries
s2.quote: 135-foot, three-masted schooner … rests upright in 117 feet of water

highlights.text: Upright schooner with intact deck and lower hull

summary.text: Upright three-masted schooner lost in 1898 and lying in 117 ft northeast of Pultneyville in the Lake Ontario national marine sanctuary. Its deck and lower hull survive, and it is among the sanctuary's more accessible wrecks.

s1.quote: The sunken vessel lies at a depth of about 105 feet (32 m) in the southern basin of Lake George … The site is accessible to the diving public with advanced diving skills.

s2.quote: 105 feet deep. … Not a beginner dive. … Lake george is cold and dark at this depth. Soft bottom can silt easily.

s3.quote: Diving the Radeau is by registration only. The Radeau Preserve is open from the second Saturday of June through Labor Day. … Auxiliary air (pony tank and regulator) are required … visibility may be extremely limited.

access.value: Registration only at the NYS DEC booth at Lake George Beach; open second Saturday of June to Labor Day; pony tank and regulator required

hazards.text: Silty soft bottom; visibility may be very limited

summary.text: Seven-sided 1758 military radeau in the Lake George state underwater preserve, at about 105 ft. Diving is by DEC registration with a pony bottle; the cold, silty site is not a beginner dive.

s1.quote: Lake Michigan, ~6.3 miles NE of Milwaukee … 120ft to 135ft (36.6 to 41.2m) … careful buoyancy is required to avoid disturbing silt
The second cave is an extensive network of both wet and dry passages that is only accessible by cave diving. … As of 2009, it has been explored to about 2200 feet.
